scenario: I live in NYC and have a dog who has developed life-threatening cancer, and I must take him regularly to the hospital for treatment. The problem is I have no car, and the hospital is very far away. The trains that run there have no-dog policies or restrict the size of the dog significantly. My dog is an eighty-pound golden retriever mutt, so he is too big for the train's size policy. The thought occurred to me to put a service dog vest on my non-service dog to pretend that he is one. And if anyone asks, I can say he is a seizure-response dog. That way, I can get on the train with him and have a reason for why he’s with me. My dog is well-behaved and has the look of a service dog, so I think I can get away with it. If I put a service dog vest on my non-service dog to pretend that he is one, then my dog can get life-saving treatment. If I do not do this, there won’t be any other way for him to get treatment, and he will die.
choice: I decide to put a service dog vest on my non-service dog to pretend that he is one
entities: i,my dog with cancer,hospital staff involved in treating my dog,train staff who may question or enforce the dog policy
outcomes: Transit staff and passengers are deceived about my dog's service-animal status
My dog and I are allowed onto the train despite the dog policy
